Term: Damaging statuses deal damage just before the affected entity's turn. They do not stack together, even if they are the same type. If an entity currently has a damaging status, they cannot be affected by a new one unless the new one is unremovable and the old one isn’t, in which case the new status overrides the old one. A damaging status is typically denoted with X (Status)/Y, which means the status deals X damage and has a duration of Y rounds. A Non-Damaging Status is typically denoted with (Status)/Y, which means the status has a duration of Y rounds. Reapplying a non damaging status restarts the status with its new specified duration.

Description: If the affected player rolls 16+ for accuracy while under the effects of Confusion, the user takes their higher offensive stat (ATK/MAG) in damage. This damage cannot be taken more than once for multi-hit moves.
Cripple is denoted with X Cripple/Y. The affected player loses X HP for every tile they willingly move while affected. This effect lasts for Y rounds.
The affected player is unable to use their movement action while affected.
The affected player can only use Basic Abilities other than Attack of Opportunity, unless the move states it can be used while sealed. Passives are unaffected.
The affected player can only move up to half their MP stat, rounded up.
The affected player is unable to use any action, including reactions, until the effect wears off. Self-inflicted stun cannot be removed or suppressed in any way.

Whenever a player with a Shield would take damage, the Shield does instead until it runs out of HP or its duration ends. While a player has a shield, abilities that target them cannot inflict non-damaging statuses. This does not remove current ones.

Buffs are always underlined and Debuffs are always italicised in ability effects.
(In general, a Buff or Debuff is a finite duration effect that increases or decreases an entity's stats, accuracy, or damage.)
